# /crav1-spark-to-spec

lane: specify | group: Start | starter: yes | stage: stable | since: 1.0.0 | prompts: 3
purpose: Turn a one- or two-sentence spark into spec.md.
use_when: You have 1–2 sentences
reads: Reads the spark and the repo.
writes: Writes `docs/specs/<slug>/spec.md`, a thin `docs/system/` including `glossary.md` when that folder is missing, otherwise one index row plus a missing glossary or new glossary rows, and `work-item.md` when the user opts in on Azure Repos. A `repos.md` it writes includes a `## Synced at` section and leaves no Synced at line. When this run read only that slice's code, writes or updates `Synced at: <repo> <branch>@<short sha>, <date>` on that slice's `spec.md` and does not touch the `## Synced at` section of `repos.md`.
leaves alone: Leaves application code and an existing landscape alone.
limits: extend edits that spec and adds no second index row. A quoted note in `docs/notes/` gets its slug in `used_by` and a `Full source:` link; notes are never absorbed.
flow:
- The closing decisions are a list, not a question, and a bare `yes` afterwards does not run the next skill.
- One-liner → questions → thin `docs/system/` when missing, including `glossary.md`, then `spec.md`, then one index row (greenfield, brownfield feature, or later feature on an existing landscape; new slug unless they extend).
- A missing `glossary.md` is filled.
- A meaning the source does not state is `to be researched`.
- On Azure Repos, offers once to write `work-item.md`.
called_by: Called by the user.
runs by itself: Calls `/crav1-create-feature-branch` when the repo already has commits.
you run next: /crav1-create-feature-branch; /crav1-review-architecture; /crav1-tighten-spec
first: `/crav1-spark-to-spec Spark: <one or two sentences> Treat this as greenfield. Do not write code. Ask questions first.`
walkthrough: from-nothing.md
human: https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/blob/v1.205.0/docs/reference/skills/crav1-spark-to-spec.md
